decisions.reason: The same message independently establishes the strapline lines and contrast options, which are already fully represented; the overall graduated-orange direction requires no additional candidate-state change.
Selecting a graduated-orange treatment does not change the task-local obligation to develop original initial concepts using references only as inspiration.
The colour direction does not alter the independently specified flame-based O or its recognition requirement.
Adopting a graduated-orange treatment does not change the requirement for fresh, original artwork or the inspiration-only role of the AI-generated draft.
The colour change does not affect the company name, exclusion of the word truck, or the broader-business representation.
The message separately establishes letterform preferences, but the overall graduated-orange treatment does not modify those typography attributes.
The graduated-orange treatment does not change the requirement to include the existing strapline.
The source selects a visual logo treatment but does not change the separate obligation to supply brand-colour documentation or provide a concrete colour specification for that deliverable.
The logo colour treatment has no necessary effect on the separate font-guidance deliverable.
